chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, stood over those killed at Badr, after he had gathered them into a pit, and he said:
"O people of the pit, indeed we have found what our Lord promised us to be true; so have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"
Then the hypocrites said, "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah is speaking to the dead."
So he looked at them and said, "If they were permitted to speak, they would say: Yes; and indeed the best provision is taqwa."

key_terms.بِبَدْرٍ: at Badr, the site of the famous battle
key_terms.ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ: taqwa; God-consciousness and piety as the best provision
key_terms.ٱلْقَلِيبِ: the pit or well into which they were gathered
key_terms.ٱلْمُنَافِقُونَ: the hypocrites who objected to addressing the dead

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the dead hearing and the importance of taqwa?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم addressing the slain of Badr after their death, affirming the truth of Allah’s promise and implying awareness in the state after death. It also concludes with a moral exhortation that the best provision is taqwa, joining a historical event with an ethical lesson about the hereafter and preparedness for it.
